article.title: Useful phrases for starting a meeting
article.description: Common professional openers: 'Shall we get started?', 'Let's dive right in.', 'Thanks everyone for making the time.', 'I'd like to run through today's agenda.' Register: professional but not overly formal — appropriate for most workplace meetings. Avoid overly casual openers like 'What's up guys' in a professional context.

generated.caption:
Ever wondered how to sound confident when starting a meeting? It's all about finding phrases that are professional but not overly formal! Instead of casual greetings, try openers like "Shall we get started?" to kick things off smoothly.

Save this for your next meeting and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily English tips!
generated.script: Professional meetings mein 'What's up guys' bolte ho kya? NO! Ye overly casual hai. Instead, use professional but not overly formal phrases. Like, start karne ke liye: 'Shall we get started?' Ya phir, 'Let's dive right in.' Everyone ko thank karne ke liye: 'Thanks everyone for making the time.' Aur agenda ke liye: 'I'd like to run through today's agenda.' Easy, right? Toh ab next time jab bhi meeting start karni ho, use these phrases. Aap confident aur prepared lagoge! Comment mein batao aapka favourite phrase kaunsa hai aur English Vault ko follow karo!

slides.body: Starting a meeting professionally sets the right tone for the discussion. Phrases like 'Shall we get started?', 'Let's dive right in,' or 'Thanks everyone for making the time' are excellent choices. They strike a balance between professional and approachable, suitable for most workplace meetings. It's important to avoid overly casual greetings like 'What's up guys' in a professional setting, opting instead for phrases such as 'I'd like to run through today's agenda' to smoothly transition into the agenda.
